_meta.indication: BRILINTA is a P2Y12 platelet inhibitor indicated to reduce the rate of thrombotic cardiovascular events in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) (unstable angina, non-ST elevation myocardial infarction, or ST elevation myocardial infarction).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, parallel-arm, multinational trial comparing ticagrelor 90 mg BID to clopidogrel 75 mg QD, both with aspirin.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) presenting within 24 hours of onset of chest pain; predominantly male (72%) and Caucasian (92%).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: composite of first occurrence of cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI (excluding silent MI), or non-fatal stroke.
pivotal_trials.result: Composite of CV death, MI, or stroke 9.8% (BRILINTA) vs 11.7% (clopidogrel), HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.77, 0.92), p=0.0003; all-cause mortality 4.5% vs 5.9%, HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.69, 0.89), p=0.0003.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions are bleeding 12% and dyspnea 14%. Non-CABG total bleeding (Major + Minor) 8.7% vs 7.0% clopidogrel; dyspnea 13.8% vs 7.8% clopidogrel.
target_moa: Ticagrelor and its major metabolite reversibly interact with the platelet P2Y12 ADP-receptor to prevent signal transduction and platelet activation.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: BLEEDING RISK — BRILINTA, like other antiplatelet agents, can cause significant, sometimes fatal, bleeding. Also WARNING: ASPIRIN DOSE AND BRILINTA EFFECTIVENESS — maintenance doses of aspirin above 100 mg reduce the effectiveness of BRILINTA and should be avoided.

rems.type: A REMS is required consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments, to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of bleeding and loss of efficacy when co-administered with maintenance doses of aspirin ≥100 mg daily.

advisory_committee.vote: The ticagrelor NDA was presented to the Cardio-Renal Advisory Committee on July 28, 2010, and by a 7-1 vote the committee recommended approval.

description.text: Added long-term secondary prevention of thrombotic events in patients with a history of myocardial infarction, based on the PEGASUS trial

citations.quote: This Prior Approval efficacy supplemental new drug application provides for the inclusion of data from the PEGASUS trial entitled, "A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled, Parallel Group, Multinational Trial, to Assess the Prevention of Thrombotic Events with Ticagrelor Compared to Placebo on a Background of Acetyl Salicylic Acid (ASA) Therapy in Patients with History of Myocardial Infarction".

description.text: Added labeling on use of ticagrelor in patients with End Stage Renal Disease on dialysis and PLLR compliance

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to labeling to include information on use of ticagrelor in patients with End Stage Renal Disease on dialysis and changes to labeling to comply with the Pregnancy Lactation and Labeling Rule.

description.text: Added indication to reduce risk of first MI or stroke in patients with coronary artery disease at high risk, established in type 2 diabetes mellitus population

citations.quote: *BRILINTA is indicated to reduce the risk of a first MI or stroke in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) at high risk for such events. While use is not limited to this setting, the efficacy of BRILINTA was established in a population with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).*

description.text: Added indication to reduce the risk of stroke in patients with acute ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤5) or high-risk TIA

citations.quote: *BRILINTA is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke in patients with acute ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale score \le 5) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA).*

description.text: Updated Section 8.4 pediatric use labeling to add conclusions from the completed HESTIA3 pediatric study

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for modifications to Section 8.4 of the U.S. Prescribing Information to add conclusions from the completed HESTIA3 pediatric study.

description.text: Labeling revised to provide guidance on discontinuation of concomitant aspirin in CAD patients who underwent PCI

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to labeling to provide guidance to prescribers regarding discontinuation of concomitant aspirin in patients with coronary artery disease who have undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Throughout the prescribing information, language advising not to exceed 100 mg of maintenance dose of aspirin has been revised because the recommended dose of concomitant aspirin is clearly stated for each indication.

summary.text: BRILINTA was approved under a traditional (non-accelerated) NDA based on the single PLATO outcomes trial, after a prior Complete Response Letter (December 16, 2010) and an Advisory Committee that voted 7 to 1 for approval; approval required a REMS and the pediatric study requirement was waived.

citations.quote: The January 20, 2011 submission constituted a complete response to our December 16, 2010, action letter.
The ticagrelor NDA was presented to the Cardio-Renal Advisory Committee on July 28, 2010. By a 7-1 vote the committee recommended approval.

In accordance with section 505-1 of the FDA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Brilinta (ticagrelor) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of bleeding and loss of efficacy when co-administered with maintenance doses of aspirin \ge 100 mg daily.
We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for this application because necessary studies are impossible or highly impracticable.
The January 20, 2011 submission constituted a complete response to our December 16, 2010, action letter.

basis.text: The Agency's position on approval was critically dependent upon the persuasiveness of the aspirin hypothesis, reflecting concern over the regional (North America/US) difference in efficacy results in PLATO.
